sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ viddhāv anyonyaśaravikṣatau rejatuḥ samare rājan puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Each having pierced the other deeply, each gashed by the other's shafts, the two of them shone in the battle, O king, like two kiṃśuka trees in full bloom.

sanskrit: alambusas tu saṃkruddhaḥ kuntibhojaśarārditaḥ aśobhata paraṃ lakṣmyā puṣpāḍhya iva kiṃśukaḥ
english: But Alambusa, enraged and tormented by Kuntibhoja's arrows, gleamed with surpassing splendor, like a kiṃśuka rich with blossoms.

sanskrit: kuntibhojaṃ tato rakṣo viddhvā bahubhir āyasaiḥ anadad bhairavaṃ nādaṃ vāhinyāḥ pramukhe tava
english: Then that demon, having pierced Kuntibhoja with many iron shafts, roared a fearsome roar at the head of your army.

sanskrit: tatas tau samare śūrau yodhayantau parasparam dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni śakrajambhau yathā purā
english: Then all beings beheld those two heroes contending against each other in the battle, as once they beheld Śakra and Jambha of old.

sanskrit: śakuniṃ rabhasaṃ yuddhe kṛtavairaṃ ca bhārata mādrīputrau ca saṃrabdhau śarair ardayatāṃ mṛdhe
english: And the two sons of Mādrī, furious in the fray, O Bhārata, tormented with their arrows the impetuous Śakuni, who had wrought enmity against them.

sanskrit: tan mūlaḥ sa mahārāja prāvartata janakṣayaḥ tvayā saṃjanito 'tyarthaṃ karṇena ca vivardhitaḥ
english: From that source, O great king, arose this destruction of men—begotten in full measure by you, and swollen yet greater by Karṇa.

sanskrit: uddhukṣitaś ca putreṇa tava krodhahutāśanaḥ ya imāṃ pṛthivīṃ rājan dagdhuṃ sarvāṃ samudyataḥ
english: And the fire of wrath was fanned to flame by your son—that fire which, O king, rose up to consume this whole earth.

sanskrit: śakuniḥ pāṇḍuputrābhyāṃ kṛtaḥ sa vimukhaḥ śaraiḥ nābhyajānata kartavyaṃ yudhi kiṃ cit parākramam
english: Turned to flight by the arrows of the two sons of Pāṇḍu, Śakuni could no longer find any feat of valor to perform in the fight.

sanskrit: vimukhaṃ cainam ālokya mādrīputrau mahārathau vavarṣatuḥ punar bāṇair yathā meghau mahāgirim
english: And seeing him put to flight, the two great warriors, the sons of Mādrī, rained their arrows upon him again, as two clouds upon a great mountain.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ saṃprāyāj javanair aśvair droṇānīkāya saubalaḥ
english: Struck down by many smooth-jointed arrows, the son of Subala sped away on his swift horses toward Droṇa's division.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tathā śūraṃ rākṣasaṃ tam alāyudham abhyayād rabhasaṃ yuddhe vegam āsthāya madhyamam
english: Ghaṭotkaca likewise advanced upon the valiant rākṣasa Alāyudha, impetuous in battle, taking up a moderate speed.

sanskrit: tayor yuddhaṃ mahārāja citrarūpam ivābhavat yādṛśaṃ hi purā vṛttaṃ rāmarāvaṇayor mṛdhe
english: The combat between those two, O great king, took on a marvelous aspect, like that which long ago passed in the fray between Rāma and Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā madrarājānam āhave viddhvā pañcāśatā bāṇaiḥ punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: Then king Yudhiṣṭhira, having pierced the king of the Madras in battle with fifty arrows, pierced him again with seven.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tayor atyadbhutaṃ nṛpa yathā pūrvaṃ mahad yuddhaṃ śambarāmararājayoḥ
english: Then there arose between those two a most wondrous combat, O lord of men, like the great battle of old between Śambara and the king of the gods.

sanskrit: viviṃśatiś citraseno vikarṇaś ca tavātmajaḥ ayodhayan bhīmasenaṃ mahatyā senayā vṛtāḥ
english: Viviṃśati, Citrasena, and your son Vikarṇa, surrounded by a great host, gave battle to Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathā tasmin pravṛtte tu saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe kauraveyāṃs tridhābhūtān pāṇḍavāḥ samupādravan
english: Saṃjaya said: When that hair-raising battle was thus joined, the Pāṇḍavas fell upon the Kauravas, who had divided themselves into three.

sanskrit: jalasaṃdhaṃ mahābāhur bhīmaseno nyavārayat yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sahānīkaḥ kṛtavarmāṇam āhave
english: The mighty-armed Bhīmasena held back Jalasaṃdha, while Yudhiṣṭhira with his host checked Kṛtavarman in the battle.

sanskrit: kirantaṃ śaravarṣāṇi rocamāna ivāṃśumān dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārāja droṇam abhyadravad raṇe
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, rushed in the fray upon Droṇa, who, pouring forth showers of arrows, shone like the radiant sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tvaratāṃ sarvadhanvinām kurūṇāṃ somakānāṃ ca saṃkruddhānāṃ parasparam
english: Then a battle arose between all those eager bowmen, the Kurus and the Somakas, each enraged against the other.

sanskrit: saṃkṣaye tu tathā bhūte vartamāne mahābhaye dvaṃdvībhūteṣu sainyeṣu yudhyamāneṣv abhītavat
english: While that fearful carnage was thus going forward, the armies, paired off in single combats, fought on fearlessly.

sanskrit: droṇaḥ pāñcālaputreṇa balī balavatā saha vicikṣepa pṛṣatkaughāṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Mighty Droṇa, contending with the mighty son of Pāñcāla, hurled torrents of shafts; it was a thing of wonder to behold.

sanskrit: puṇḍarīkavanānīva vidhvastāni samantataḥ cakrāte droṇapāñcālyau nṛṇāṃ śīrṣāṇy anekaśaḥ
english: Droṇa and the Pāñcāla strewed the heads of men in multitudes all around, like beds of white lotuses laid waste on every side.

sanskrit: vinikīrṇāni vīrāṇām anīkeṣu samantataḥ vastrābharaṇaśastrāṇi dhvajavarmāyudhāni ca
english: Scattered all about among the ranks lay the garments, ornaments, and weapons of the heroes, their banners, armor, and arms.

sanskrit: tapanīyavicitrāṅgāḥ saṃsiktā rudhireṇa ca saṃsaktā iva dṛśyante meghasaṃghāḥ savidyutaḥ
english: With bodies adorned in bright gold and drenched in blood, they appeared like masses of clouds clinging together, lit with lightning.

sanskrit: kuñjarāśvanarān saṃkhye pātayantaḥ patatribhiḥ tālamātrāṇi cāpāni vikarṣanto mahārathāḥ
english: The great warriors, drawing bows as tall as palm trees, felled elephants, horses, and men in the battle with their winged shafts.

sanskrit: asicarmāṇi cāpāni śirāṃsi kavacāni ca viprakīryanta śūrāṇāṃ saṃprahāre mahātmanām
english: Swords and shields, bows, heads, and coats of mail were scattered abroad in the onslaught of those great-souled heroes.

sanskrit: utthitāny agaṇeyāni kabandhāni samantataḥ adṛśyanta mahārāja tasmin paramasaṃkule
english: Countless headless trunks, risen upright on every side, were seen, O great king, in that utmost tumult.

sanskrit: gṛdhrāḥ kaṅkā vaḍāḥ śyenā vāyasā jambukās tathā bahavaḥ piśitāśāś ca tatrādṛśyanta māriṣa
english: Vultures, herons, kites, hawks, crows, and jackals, and many other flesh-eating creatures, were seen there, O honored one.

sanskrit: bhakṣayantaḥ sma māṃsāni pibantaś cāpi śoṇitam vilumpantaḥ sma keśāṃś ca majjāś ca bahudhā nṛpa
english: They devoured the flesh and drank the blood, and tore away the hair and marrow in many ways, O king.

sanskrit: ākarṣantaḥ śarīrāṇi śarīrāvayavāṃs tathā narāśvagajasaṃghānāṃ śirāṃsi ca tatas tataḥ
english: They dragged about the corpses, and the severed limbs, and the heads of multitudes of men, horses, and elephants, hither and thither.

sanskrit: kṛtāstrā raṇadīkṣābhir dīkṣitāḥ śaradhāriṇaḥ raṇe jayaṃ prārthayanto bhṛśaṃ yuyudhire tadā
english: The skilled archers, consecrated by the vows of battle and bearing their arrows, fought fiercely then, longing for victory in the fray.

sanskrit: asimārgān bahuvidhān vicerus tāvakā raṇe ṛṣṭibhiḥ śaktibhiḥ prāsaiḥ śūlatomarapaṭṭiśaiḥ
english: Your warriors plied many kinds of sword-strokes in the battle, with double-edged swords, lances, javelins, pikes, darts, and tridents.

sanskrit: gadābhiḥ parighaiś cānye vyāyudhāś ca bhujair api anyonyaṃ jaghnire kruddhā yuddharaṅgagatā narāḥ
english: Others, with maces and iron bars, and some even weaponless with bare arms, smote one another in their fury, those men come to the arena of war.

sanskrit: rathino rathibhiḥ sārdham aśvārohāś ca sādibhiḥ mātaṅgā varamātaṅgaiḥ padātāś ca padātibhiḥ
english: Car-warriors closed with car-warriors, horsemen with horsemen, mighty elephants with mighty elephants, and foot-soldiers with foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: kṣībā ivānye conmattā raṅgeṣv iva ca cāraṇāḥ uccukruśus tathānyonyaṃ jaghnur anyonyam āhave
english: Others, as if drunk and frenzied, like minstrels upon the stage, shouted aloud at one another and slew one another in the battle.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathā yuddhe nirmaryāde viśāṃ pate dhṛṣṭadyumno hayān aśvair droṇasya vyatyamiśrayat
english: As that lawless battle was being waged, O lord of the people, Dhṛṣṭadyumna mingled his own horses with the horses of Droṇa.

sanskrit: te hayā sādhv aśobhanta vimiśrā vātaraṃhasaḥ pārāvatasavarṇāś ca raktaśoṇāś ca saṃyuge hayāḥ śuśubhire rājan meghā iva savidyutaḥ
english: Those horses, swift as the wind, shone splendidly thus commingled; dove-colored and blood-red, the steeds in that encounter gleamed, O king, like clouds shot through with lightning.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca saṃprekṣya droṇam abhyāśam āgatam asicarmādade vīro dhanur utsṛjya bhārata
english: And the hero Dhṛṣṭadyumna, seeing Droṇa come close at hand, cast aside his bow and took up sword and shield, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: cikīrṣur duṣkaraṃ karma pārṣataḥ paravīrahā īṣayā samatikramya droṇasya ratham āviśat
english: The son of Pṛṣata, slayer of hostile heroes, resolved to perform a difficult feat, and stepping across the chariot-pole, he mounted into Droṇa's car.

sanskrit: atiṣṭhad yugamadhye sa yugasaṃnahaneṣu ca jaghānārdheṣu cāśvānāṃ tat sainyāny abhyapūjayan
english: He stood in the midst of the yoke and upon the lashings of the yoke, and struck at the flanks of the horses; the armies applauded that deed.

sanskrit: khaḍgena caratas tasya śoṇāśvān adhitiṣṭhataḥ na dadarśāntaraṃ droṇas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: As he ranged about with his sword, treading upon the red horses, Droṇa could find no opening against him; it was a thing of wonder.

sanskrit: yathā śyenasya patanaṃ vaneṣv āmiṣagṛddhinaḥ tathaivāsīd abhīsāras tasya droṇaṃ jighāṃsataḥ
english: As the swoop of a hawk greedy for flesh in the woods, so was his onset as he sought to slay Droṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatenāsya śatacandraṃ samākṣipat droṇo drupadaputrasya khaḍgaṃ ca daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Droṇa shattered with a hundred shafts the hundred-mooned shield of Drupada's son, and his sword with ten arrows.

sanskrit: hayāṃś caiva catuḥṣaṣṭyā śarāṇāṃ jaghnivān balī dhvajaṃ chatraṃ ca bhallābhyāṃ tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī
english: And the mighty one slew his horses with sixty-four arrows, and with two broad-headed shafts struck down his banner and his parasol and both his flank-charioteers.

sanskrit: athāsmai tvarito bāṇam aparaṃ jīvitāntakam ākarṇapūrṇaṃ cikṣepa vajraṃ vajradharo yathā
english: Then in haste he loosed at him another arrow, a bringer of death, drawn back full to the ear, as the wielder of the thunderbolt hurls his bolt.

sanskrit: taṃ caturdaśabhir bāṇair bāṇaṃ ciccheda sātyakiḥ grastam ācāryamukhyena dhṛṣṭadyumnam amocayat
english: Sātyaki cut that arrow apart with fourteen arrows, and so released Dhṛṣṭadyumna, who had been seized by the foremost of preceptors.

sanskrit: siṃheneva mṛgaṃ grastaṃ narasiṃhena māriṣa droṇena mocayām āsa pāñcālyaṃ śinipuṃgavaḥ
english: As a deer seized by a lion, so was the Pāñcāla seized by that lion among men, Droṇa; and the bull of Śini's line, that lion among men, set him free, O honored one.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ prekṣya goptāraṃ pāñcālyasya mahāhave śarāṇāṃ tvarito droṇaḥ ṣaḍviṃśatyā samarpayat
english: Seeing Sātyaki the protector of the Pāñcāla in that great battle, Droṇa swiftly assailed him with twenty-six arrows.

sanskrit: tato droṇaṃ śineḥ pautro grasantam iva sṛñjayān pratyavidhyac chitair bāṇaiḥ ṣaḍviṃśatyā stanāntare
english: Then the grandson of Śini struck back at Droṇa, who was as if devouring the Sṛñjayas, piercing him in the breast with twenty-six sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve rathās tūrṇaṃ pāñcālā jayagṛddhinaḥ sātvatābhisṛte droṇe dhṛṣṭadyumnam amocayan
english: Then, when the Sātvata had thus assailed Droṇa, all the Pāñcāla car-warriors, eager for victory, swiftly delivered Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bāṇe tasmin nikṛtte tu dhṛṣṭadyumne ca mokṣite tena vṛṣṇipravīreṇa yuyudhānena saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that arrow had been cut down and Dhṛṣṭadyumna had been set free by that foremost hero of the Vṛṣṇis, by Yuyudhāna, O Saṃjaya—

sanskrit: amarṣito maheṣvāsaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ naravyāghraḥ śineḥ pautre droṇaḥ kim akarod yudhi
english: —what did that great archer Droṇa, the tiger among men, foremost of all bearers of arms, filled with indignation, do against the grandson of Śini in the fight?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saṃpradrutaḥ krodhaviṣo vyāditāsyaśarāsanaḥ tīkṣṇadhāreṣudaśanaḥ śitanārācadaṃṣṭravān
english: Saṃjaya said: Rushing forward, his venom of wrath upraised, his bow a gaping mouth, his teeth the keen-edged arrows, his fangs the whetted iron shafts—

sanskrit: saṃrambhāmarṣatāmrākṣo mahāhir iva niḥśvasan naravīrapramuditaiḥ śoṇair aśvair mahājavaiḥ
english: —his eyes red with fury and resentment, hissing like a great serpent, with his red horses of great speed, rejoicing among heroic men—

sanskrit: utpatadbhir ivākāśaṃ kramadbhir iva sarvataḥ rukmapuṅkhāñ śarān asyan yuyudhānam upādravat
english: —as though leaping up to the sky, as though striding over all things, he sped upon Yuyudhāna, hurling gold-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: śarapātamahāvarṣaṃ rathaghoṣabalāhakam kārmukākarṣavikṣiptaṃ nārācabahuvidyutam
english: With its great downpour of falling arrows, with the rumble of chariots for its thundercloud, scattered abroad by the drawing of bows, lit with the lightning of its many iron shafts—

sanskrit: śaktikhaḍgāśanidharaṃ krodhavegasamutthitam droṇamegham anāvāryaṃ hayamārutacoditam
english: —bearing spears, swords, and bolts, risen up in the rush of his wrath, that irresistible cloud of Droṇa, driven on by the wind of his horses.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaivābhipatantaṃ taṃ śūraḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ uvāca sūtaṃ śaineyaḥ prahasan yuddhadurmadaḥ
english: Seeing him bearing down thus, the heroic grandson of Śini, conqueror of hostile cities, mad with the lust of battle, said to his charioteer, laughing aloud:

sanskrit: etaṃ vai brāhmaṇaṃ krūraṃ svakarmaṇy anavasthitam āśrayaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya rājño duḥkhabhayāvaham
english: "This cruel brahmin, who keeps not to his own appointed duty, the refuge of king Dhārtarāṣṭra, the bringer of sorrow and fear—

sanskrit: śīghraṃ prajavitair aśvaiḥ pratyudyāhi prahṛṣṭavat ācāryaṃ rājaputrāṇāṃ satataṃ śūramāninam
english: "—drive swiftly forth with hastening horses, joyfully, to meet this preceptor of the princes, who ever deems himself a hero."

sanskrit: tato rajatasaṃkāśā mādhavasya hayottamāḥ droṇasyābhimukhāḥ śīghram agacchan vātaraṃhasaḥ
english: Then the excellent horses of the Mādhava, silver-bright and swift as the wind, advanced quickly to face Droṇa.

sanskrit: iṣujālāvṛtaṃ ghoram andhakāram anantaram anādhṛṣyam ivānyeṣāṃ śūrāṇām abhavat tadā
english: Then there came a dreadful, unbroken darkness, veiled by a net of arrows, that seemed unassailable to all other heroes.

sanskrit: tataḥ śīghrāstraviduṣor droṇasātvatayos tadā nāntaraṃ śaravṛṣṭīnāṃ dṛśyate narasiṃhayoḥ
english: Then, between Droṇa and the Sātvata, those two lions among men skilled in swift weaponry, no gap could be seen in the showers of their arrows.

sanskrit: iṣūṇāṃ saṃnipātena śabdo dhārābhighātajaḥ śuśruve śakramuktānām aśanīnām iva svanaḥ
english: From the clashing together of the arrows there arose a sound, born of the striking of their streams, that was heard like the roar of thunderbolts loosed by Śakra.

sanskrit: nārācair atividdhānāṃ śarāṇāṃ rūpam ābabhau āśīviṣavidaṣṭānāṃ sarpāṇām iva bhārata
english: The aspect of the arrows pierced deeply by the iron shafts shone forth, O Bhārata, like that of serpents bitten by venomous snakes.

sanskrit: tayor jyātalanirghoṣo vyaśrūyata sudāruṇaḥ ajasraṃ śailaśṛṅgāṇāṃ vajreṇāhanyatām iva
english: The dreadful clamor of their bowstrings and palm-guards was heard unceasingly, as of mountain-peaks struck again and again by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: ubhayos tau rathau rājaṃs te cāśvāstau ca sārathī rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śaraiś channāś citrarūpā babhus tadā
english: The chariots of both, O king, their horses and their charioteers, covered with gold-feathered arrows, then shone forth in wondrous forms.

sanskrit: nirmalānām ajihmānāṃ nārācānāṃ viśāṃ pate nirmuktāśīviṣābhānāṃ saṃpāto 'bhūt sudāruṇaḥ
english: Most terrible, O lord of the people, was the falling together of those bright, straight iron shafts, that gleamed like venomous serpents loosed from their sloughs.

sanskrit: ubhayoḥ patite chatre tathaiva patitau dhvajau ubhau rudhirasiktāṅgāv ubhau ca vijayaiṣiṇau
english: The parasols of both were struck down, and likewise both their banners fell; both had their limbs bathed in blood, and both were eager for victory.

sanskrit: sravadbhiḥ śoṇitaṃ gātraiḥ prasrutāv iva vāraṇau anyonyam abhividhyetāṃ jīvitāntakaraiḥ śaraiḥ
english: With their limbs streaming blood, like two elephants in rut, they pierced each other with arrows that bring life to its end.

sanskrit: garjitotkruṣṭasaṃnādāḥ śaṅkhadundubhinisvanāḥ upāraman mahārāja vyājahāra na kaś cana
english: The roars, the shouts, the clamor, and the sound of conches and drums fell silent, O great king; no one spoke a word.

sanskrit: tūṣṇīṃbhūtāny anīkāni yodhā yuddhād upāraman dadṛśe dvairathaṃ tābhyāṃ jātakautūhalo janaḥ
english: The hosts fell still, the warriors ceased from fighting, and the people, filled with wonder, gazed upon the single combat of those two.

sanskrit: rathino hastiyantāro hayārohāḥ padātayaḥ avaikṣantācalair netraiḥ parivārya ratharṣabhau
english: Car-warriors, elephant-drivers, horsemen, and foot-soldiers, encircling those two bulls among chariot-fighters, looked on with unwavering eyes.

sanskrit: hastyanīkāny atiṣṭhanta tathānīkāni vājinām tathaiva rathavāhinyaḥ prativyūhya vyavasthitāḥ
english: The divisions of elephants stood still, and so the divisions of horse, and the chariot-columns too stood ranged in their array.

sanskrit: muktāvidrumacitraiś ca maṇikāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ dhvajair ābharaṇaiś citraiḥ kavacaiś ca hiraṇmayaiḥ
english: With banners bright with pearl and coral and adorned with gems and gold, with brilliant ornaments and golden coats of mail,

sanskrit: vaijayantīpatākābhiḥ paristomāṅgakambalaiḥ vimalair niśitaiḥ śastrair hayānāṃ ca prakīrṇakaiḥ
english: with victory-pennons and flags, with caparisons and body-cloths, with bright and whetted weapons, and with the tail-fans of the horses,

sanskrit: jātarūpamayībhiś ca rājatībhiś ca mūrdhasu gajānāṃ kumbhamālābhir dantaveṣṭaiś ca bhārata
english: and with frontlets of gold and silver upon the brows of the elephants, and the wreaths upon their temple-bosses and the bands about their tusks, O Bhārata—

sanskrit: sabalākāḥ sakhadyotāḥ sairāvataśatahradāḥ adṛśyantoṣṇaparyāye meghānām iva vāgurāḥ
english: —they appeared, with their cranes and fireflies, with their rainbows and lightnings, like the gathering nets of clouds in the season of heat.

sanskrit: apaśyann asmadīyāś ca te ca yaudhiṣṭhirāḥ sthitāḥ tad yuddhaṃ yuyudhānasya droṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Both our men and the followers of Yudhiṣṭhira stood and watched that combat of Yuyudhāna and of the great-souled Droṇa.

sanskrit: vimānāgragatā devā brahmaśakrapurogamāḥ siddhacāraṇasaṃghāś ca vidyādharamahoragāḥ
english: The gods, with Brahmā and Śakra at their head, borne aloft in the foremost of celestial cars, and the hosts of Siddhas and Cāraṇas, the Vidyādharas and the great serpents,
